# MapMyCells Cell Neighborhoods Across seqFISH Brain Sections

## Overview

This analysis updates the original cell-localization workflow to use Allen
MapMyCells subclass and supertype assignments from the latest seqFISH Seurat
object. Neighborhoods are defined within 60 µm and summarized separately for
all cells in each section and for the existing manually drawn anatomical
regions. The primary analysis requires MapMyCells bootstrap probability ≥ 0.5;
all assigned labels are retained as a sensitivity analysis. An exploratory
ROI-section analysis tests SPF–WildR differences with imaging run blocked; it
does not replace an animal-level analysis.

```{r}
#| label: display-stats
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

cat("::: {.stat-row}\n")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[1,086,336]{.stat-value}\n[Whole-slice cells]{.stat-label}\n:::\n")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[443,663]{.stat-value}\n[Manually gated cells]{.stat-label}\n:::\n")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[10]{.stat-value}\n[Anatomical gates]{.stat-label}\n:::\n")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[", n_complete, "/", n_jobs,
    "]{.stat-value}\n[Jobs complete]{.stat-label}\n:::\n", sep = "")
cat(":::\n")
```

## Background

The original analysis used broad SingleR classes and repeatedly calculated
dense pairwise distance matrices for each query class. V2 instead uses the
MapMyCells hierarchy already stored in
[data/interim/seurat/seqFISH/merged_roi_seurat_prenorm_2026-02-16.rds]{.path},
finds radius neighbors once per spatial unit, and reports neighborhoods at
subclass and supertype resolution.

Whole-slice summaries include every cell in the latest Seurat object. Anatomical
summaries use `final_gate` calls joined by `cell_id` from
[data/interim/gated-seurat-metadata_2024-12-31.rds]{.path}. All 977,050 cells in
that older metadata match the latest object exactly, and 443,663 have a
non-empty final gate. The project does not contain an ROI-to-animal key, so the
SPF–WildR section uses one observation per ROI section and is explicitly
exploratory. It improves on V1's cell-level mixed model by removing cell-level
pseudoreplication, blocking imaging run, treating eligible absent pairs as
zeros, and correcting for multiple testing.

## Results

### MapMyCells confidence retention

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
![](../figures/CellNeighborhoods/CellNeighborhoods_MapMyCells_confidence_retention.png)

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 1.**]{.fig-num} Fraction of cells retained by the primary MapMyCells
bootstrap-probability threshold (≥ 0.5), shown for subclass and supertype labels
in whole slices and each manually drawn anatomical region.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Whole-slice retention is 82.1% at subclass and 89.1% at supertype level.
- Subclass retention varies most across gates (74.5% in AMYG_CT to 94.3% in
  THAL); supertype retention ranges from 81.9% in CAUD to 97.3% in RT.
- The all-label sensitivity output preserves every assignment, allowing direct
  assessment of whether confidence filtering changes a neighborhood pattern.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-confidence`](#cell-fig-confidence){.provenance}
:::

### Whole-slice subclass neighborhoods

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
![](../figures/CellNeighborhoods/CellNeighborhoods_MapMyCells_whole_slice_subclass_heatmap.png)

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2.**]{.fig-num} Mean local relative abundance for the 15 most abundant
MapMyCells subclasses across all 16 whole sections. Rows are query subclasses
and columns are neighbor subclasses; the primary confidence-filtered labels are
used.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Same-subclass clustering dominates: CHOR (mean local fraction 0.73), DG Glut
  (0.61), and L2/3 IT PIR–ENTl Glut (0.51) have the strongest diagonals among
  the 15 most abundant subclasses.
- Astro-TE is the most abundant confident subclass and is a recurrent neighbor
  of both neuronal and immune query populations.
- Values are descriptive averages across ROI sections, not animal-level effect
  estimates.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-whole-slice`](#cell-fig-whole-slice){.provenance}
:::

### Supertype self-neighborhoods within anatomical gates

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
![](../figures/CellNeighborhoods/CellNeighborhoods_MapMyCells_manual_gate_supertype_self_neighborhood.png)

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 3.**]{.fig-num} Mean same-supertype relative abundance within each
manually drawn anatomical region for the 20 most abundant supertypes. Empty
combinations were not observed in that region.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- The strongest self-neighborhoods match the hand-drawn anatomy: hippocampal
  CA1–ProS Glut_1 (0.52) and DG Glut_2 (0.50), BLA
  LA–BLA–BMA–PA Glut_3 (0.44), RT Gnb3 Gaba_5 (0.44), and SSC L4/5 IT CTX
  Glut_2 (0.43).
- Same-supertype abundance is summarized per ROI before pooling, so large ROIs
  do not contribute one row per cell to the displayed value.
- Group comparisons remain intentionally deferred until ROI sections can be
  mapped to animals.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-manual-gates`](#cell-fig-manual-gates){.provenance}
:::

### Exploratory SPF–WildR differences

::: {.callout-warning}
**ROI sections are not documented animals.** These tests use one value per ROI
section and block imaging run, but they are not valid animal-level inference if
multiple sections came from the same mouse. The four poor-quality sections
excluded in V1 are also excluded here, leaving six SPF and six WildR sections.
:::

```{r}
#| label: display-group-stats
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

if (has_group_results && !is.null(group_global) && !is.null(group_hits)) {
  primary_global <- group_global[label_set == "primary_confident"]
  min_global_p <- min(primary_global$permutation_p)
  min_global_fdr <- min(primary_global$global_fdr)
  cat("::: {.stat-row}\n")
  cat("::: {.stat}\n[32,889]{.stat-value}\n[Primary pairs tested]{.stat-label}\n:::\n")
  cat("::: {.stat}\n[", nrow(primary_global),
      "]{.stat-value}\n[Global families]{.stat-label}\n:::\n", sep = "")
  cat("::: {.stat}\n[", nrow(group_hits),
      "]{.stat-value}\n[Within-family FDR < 0.10]{.stat-label}\n:::\n", sep = "")
  cat("::: {.stat}\n[0]{.stat-value}\n[Study-wide FDR < 0.10]{.stat-label}\n:::\n")
  cat(":::\n")
}
```

The primary test uses `asin(sqrt(mean_rel_abund)) ~ run + group` with limma
empirical-Bayes moderation. A pair enters only when both cell types have at
least 20 cells, each group contributes at least half its available sections
(minimum three), and at least three imaging runs are represented. Exact
run-stratified label permutations test each region × taxonomy family jointly.

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
![](../figures/CellNeighborhoods/CellNeighborhoods_SPF-WildR_global_permutation_r3.png)

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 4.**]{.fig-num} Family-level omnibus tests for SPF–WildR neighborhood
differences. Each point summarizes all eligible query→neighbor pairs within one
scope, anatomical region and taxonomy level; permutations preserve the observed
SPF/WildR counts within imaging run.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- No primary family survives correction across the 22 whole-slice/manual-gate
  subclass and supertype families (minimum global FDR = 0.41).
- AMYG_BLA supertype is the strongest nominal family (exact p = 1/54 = 0.019),
  but it is not significant after family-level correction.
- The global result does not support a coherent SPF–WildR shift in neighborhood
  composition at either MapMyCells resolution.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-group-global`](#cell-fig-group-global){.provenance}
:::

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
![](../figures/CellNeighborhoods/CellNeighborhoods_SPF-WildR_top_effects_r3.png)

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 5.**]{.fig-num} Run-adjusted WildR−SPF differences for the 30
smallest moderated p-values. Intervals are 95% empirical-Bayes confidence
intervals on the raw mean local relative-abundance scale. Filled points pass
FDR < 0.10 within their own region × level family.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Seven primary pairs pass FDR within their own family, including five CAUD
  pairs, one AMYG_CT pair and one HIPP pair.
- None survives correction across all 32,889 primary pairs (minimum study-wide
  FDR = 0.88), and no parent family is globally significant.
- These isolated effects are hypothesis-generating only. The strongest include
  lower CAUD STR D1→D2 proximity in WildR and higher HIPP
  Microglia→CA1–ProS proximity, each based on only 3–6 ROI sections per group.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-group-effects`](#cell-fig-group-effects){.provenance}
:::

```{r}
#| label: display-group-hits
#| echo: false

if (!is.null(group_hits) && nrow(group_hits)) {
  display_hits <- group_hits[
    ,
    .(
      Region = region,
      Level = level,
      Query = query_name,
      Neighbor = neighbor_name,
      `WildR-SPF` = sprintf("%.3f", delta_raw_adjusted),
      `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", delta_raw_ci_low, delta_raw_ci_high),
      `Family FDR` = format.pval(fdr_family, digits = 2),
      `Study-wide FDR` = format.pval(fdr_studywide, digits = 2)
    )
  ]
  knitr::kable(
    display_hits,
    caption = "Primary pairs passing FDR < 0.10 within their own family. None passes study-wide FDR."
  )
}
```

[Source: cell `cell-tbl-group-hits`](#cell-tbl-group-hits){.provenance}

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
![](../figures/CellNeighborhoods/CellNeighborhoods_SPF-WildR_confidence_sensitivity_r3.png)

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 6.**]{.fig-num} Concordance of run-adjusted effect estimates between
the primary bootstrap ≥ 0.5 analysis and the all-label sensitivity analysis.
Point size is the number of matched query→neighbor pairs.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- Confidence-filter sensitivity is generally strong: median Spearman ρ = 0.91
  across 22 scope × region × level families (range 0.72–0.99).
- Median effect-direction agreement is 88.8%, so the null global conclusion is
  not driven by the bootstrap threshold.
- Mapping-confidence robustness does not solve the missing animal identity;
  animal-level confirmation remains required.
:::

[Source: cell `cell-fig-group-sensitivity`](#cell-fig-group-sensitivity){.provenance}
:::

The aggregated descriptive results are stored at
[data/interim/cell_neighborhoods_mapmycells/2026-11-06/cell_neighborhood_roi_summary_2026-11-06.rds]{.path}
and exported to

Per-cell sparse neighborhood summaries remain in the individual job artifacts
under [data/interim/cell_neighborhoods_mapmycells/2026-11-06/jobs/]{.path}.
The final exploratory group-test object is
[data/interim/cell_neighborhoods_mapmycells/2026-11-06/cell_neighborhood_spf_wildr_roi_exploratory_r3_2026-11-06.rds]{.path};
pairwise and global tables are under [tables/CellNeighborhoods/]{.path}.

## Next Steps

- **Done:** replaced SingleR classes with MapMyCells subclass and supertype
  assignments and analyzed whole slices plus ten manually drawn regions.
- **Done:** made bootstrap ≥ 0.5 the primary label set and retained all-label
  sensitivity outputs.
- **Done:** tested SPF–WildR differences at the ROI-section level with run
  blocking, empirical-Bayes moderation, exact family-level permutations and
  both within-family and study-wide FDR.
- Add the ROI-to-animal map and rerun the seven isolated within-family leads;
  the current global and study-wide results are null.
- Prespecify the CAUD D1/D2 and HIPP Microglia→CA1–ProS pairs before
  animal-level confirmation rather than screening the complete pair set again.

# Code & Provenance {.code-appendix}

The heavy analysis is implemented in
[notebooks/R_scripts/run_cell_localization_analysis_v2.R]{.path}. Rendering this
notebook never submits jobs or recomputes neighborhoods because
`run_analysis <- FALSE`. Array logs are under
[.cluster_runs/cell_neighborhoods_mapmycells/]{.path}; all 161 tasks in jobs
`6356434` and `6356253` completed, followed by aggregation/figure job `6356436`.
Exploratory group testing is implemented in
[notebooks/R_scripts/run_cell_neighborhood_group_tests_v2.R]{.path}. Final job
`6369866` produced revision `r3`; jobs `6361649` and `6368516` are retained as
superseded development runs (non-estimable sparse pairs/global-statistic fix,
then addition of study-wide FDR, respectively).

The notebook was rendered from `notebooks/` with the `spatialomics` Quarto and
R installation. This conda Quarto build requires its packaged share directory
to be supplied explicitly:

```bash
PATH=/resnick/groups/MazmanianLab/jboktor/software/miniforge3/envs/spatialomics/bin:${PATH} \
QUARTO_SHARE_PATH=/resnick/groups/MazmanianLab/jboktor/software/miniforge3/envs/spatialomics/share/quarto \
/resnick/groups/MazmanianLab/jboktor/software/miniforge3/envs/spatialomics/bin/quarto \
render 0X_Cell-Neighborhoods-V2_SeqFISH.qmd --to html
```
